title: Find the missing note
hook: A complete-looking page can still lack the detail you need.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that covering a note and rebuilding it from memory shows which details are missing, which reading it through cannot

misconception: Rereading a complete-looking note shows whether you know it.
objective: Reconstruct a missing field from a short source note.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: A complete-looking page can still lack the detail you need. Which check tests whether the missing details are known? Correct option: Cover then reconstruct. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and pure rules in studyModels.ts. All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The note has three named fields. Reconstructing their values makes missing details visible; this is a local completeness check.
claims.source: Roediger & Karpicke (2006), Test-Enhanced Learning, Psychological Science 17(3),249–255, DOI10.1111/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x; publisher abstract retrieved 2026-10-13: https://www.psychologicalscience.org/journals/psychological-science/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x/ . Prose-passage experiments found delayed retention advantages for retrieval over restudy. This short exercise does not establish that effect for the learner. Fixture mappings and rules are explicit conventions, not empirical demonstrations. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Every displayed result is computed from the visible exercise state: recall. One short reconstruction; not a retention experiment. The reveal reports this same state and never translates its score into a personal productivity or memory benefit.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/studyModels.ts and src/components/lifehacks/StudyLesson.tsx, note-gap-check fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts. Stage rules: check reconstructed token positions against the covered target; count exact matches out of three. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Reconstructing each value exposes the specific gap; a complete-looking note can still hide one you could not produce.

recall.question: Your meeting note has three fields: room, day and code. How do you find a value you do not actually know?
options: Cover the values and fill each field from memory
Reread the note slowly until it feels familiar
Check that each of the three fields has a value
recall.why: Reconstructing each value exposes the specific gap; a complete-looking note can still hide one you could not produce.
